title: Beef Stew
subtitle: fall-apart beef, potatoes and carrots in a thick, savoury gravy — slow Sunday comfort
imageAlt: Hearty beef stew with potatoes and carrots in a thick gravy, with crusty bread
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 3–4 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen beef? Thaw in the fridge overnight (24 h).
Use your heaviest pot (Dutch oven) — it browns better and won't scorch.
Oven option: heat to 160°C (325°F) and braise covered in the oven instead of the stovetop.
It's mostly hands-off: about 2½ hours of gentle simmering.

steps.title: Season and flour
steps.text: Pat the beef very dry, season with salt and pepper, and toss with the flour until lightly coated.

steps.title: Brown in batches
steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high. Brown the beef in 2–3 batches, 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply browned (don't crowd it or it steams). Move to a plate.

steps.title: Onions and paste
steps.text: Lower to medium, add the last 1 tbsp oil and the onions; cook 5 minutes, scraping up the brown bits. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until the paste darkens.

steps.title: Simmer low and slow
steps.text: Pour in the broth, scraping the bottom, then add the Worcestershire, thyme, bay leaves, sugar and the beef with its juices. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low (or in a 160°C / 325°F oven) 1½ hours, stirring now and then.

steps.title: Add the veg
steps.text: Add the potatoes and carrots, pushing them under the liquid. Cover and simmer 45–60 minutes more until the beef is fork-tender and the vegetables are soft.

steps.title: Thicken and season
steps.text: Take out the bay leaves. If you want it thicker, simmer uncovered 10 minutes or mash a few potato pieces into the gravy. Taste and add salt and pepper until it's well seasoned. Serve with crusty bread.

fixIt.fix: It needs more time, not less — chuck turns tender after about 2–2½ hours at a gentle simmer. Keep going in 15-minute stretches.
Simmer uncovered 10–15 minutes, or stir in 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water and bubble 1 minute.
Salt is usually the answer; a splash more Worcestershire adds depth.
Yukon Golds hold their shape better than russets; add them for the last 45 minutes only.

saleTip: Stewing beef is often ~$15–17/kg on sale at No Frills; a whole chuck roast you cube yourself is sometimes cheaper per kilo.
swap: Add a cup of frozen peas & carrots at the end if you like peas. Slow cooker: brown everything first, then cook on low 8 hours with the veg added at the start.
leftovers: Fridge 4 days — it tastes even better on day two. Freeze up to 3 months (potatoes soften slightly).
doneness: Beef is done when fork-tender (well past 71°C / 160°F). Reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested beef stew methods (Once Upon a Chef, Simply Recipes): floured, batch-browned chuck braised in broth with tomato paste and Worcestershire, vegetables added partway.
gear: Dutch oven or heavy pot with lid (5–6 L)
prepAhead: Make the whole stew a day ahead — it thickens and the flavour deepens overnight.
Cube the beef and chop the vegetables up to 1 day ahead.
reheat: Stovetop over medium-low, covered, stirring now and then, with a splash of broth or water, until steaming (74°C / 165°F). Microwave 2–3 min per bowl, stirring halfway.

basic.note: Beef, potatoes and carrots in a simple broth gravy.

stepNotes.3: Basic: broth, thyme and the beef — no Worcestershire, bay or sugar.

fancy.note: Deep, glossy bistro stew: extra tomato paste caramelised, pearl onions, a knob of butter and crusty bread.

items.name: butter
items.note: stirred in at the end for gloss

stepNotes.2: Fancy: let the tomato paste darken to a brick colour, 2–3 minutes.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: add the pearl onions with the potatoes.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Off the heat, stir in the butter and balsamic until glossy. Serve in wide bowls with warm torn crusty bread.

plating: Wide shallow bowls show off the chunks.
Beef on top, vegetables peeking around.
Torn bread on the side, never on top.

why.0-3: Flour browns with the beef and thickens the gravy as it simmers.
why.1-2: Tomato paste gives colour and a rich, savoury depth.
why.1-4: Worcestershire adds tang and savoury depth; skip it and add a little extra salt.

funFact: Stew beef turns tender only with long, slow cooking: its tough connective tissue (collagen) slowly melts into gelatin, which is also what gives the gravy its body.

keeps.note: the potatoes soften a little — still lovely
